newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Dow hoists Australian stocks to record close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Dow hoists Australian stocks to record close.

text.p: *Shares ended at a record close after the Dow posted its highest closing level on Friday. Volume 344.9 million shares, value A$542.7 million, 1,107 stocks traded, 321 steady, 459 up, 327 down.

Another strong session from Wall Street combined with hopes of a further local interest rate cut boosted the Australian share market to a record close on Monday. The benchmark All Ordinaries index finished 8.7 points firmer at 2,444.2, eclipsing its previous record close of 2,348.2 which was set on January 15.
The market also set a new intra-day life-time high of 2,456.7, 12.5 points higher than its previous life high of 2,444.2 which was also set on January 15.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the March share price index was up 10 points at 2,454, a 9.8 point premium to the index.
"The market seemed to lose a bit of its early enthusiasm after lunch. I think a bit of caution crept in when the Nikkei strated to slide again," a Sydney-based broker said.
The dealer said the day's turnover of about A$550 million was relatively light and the market's gains to lunch partly reflected the reluctance of investors to sell stock.
"There is a greater anticipation that the Reserve Bank will move to cut rates in the near future and this was backed up by the stronger local bond market," the dealer said.
The foundation for the market's rise was solid support for major bank issues, National Australia, Commonwealth and ANZ.

Apart from the possibility of lower interest rates, dealers said the interest in bank issues was also partly due to speculation that one or more of the majors could issue a special dividend or buy back shares to return excess capital.
Amongst resource issues, the gold sector was the strongest after the price of gold retraced some of its recent heavy fall in trading on London and New York commodity markets on Friday.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade remained quiet in line with the slow business in the physical market.

In other local markets, Australian bonds closed firmer after an opening flurry saw them break through key resistance. News of a small rise in December imports had little effect on the market although the market finished off its early highs.
The yield on ten-year T-bonds closed at 7.32 percent, down 0.09 percentage points from its closing level on Friday.
The Australian dollar made a mild recovery to gingerly try resistance above the 78 cent level as world foreign exchange markets focused on other major currencies.
At 4.55 p.m. (0555 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7800/05, after reaching an intra-day high of US$0.7821.

Major bank's shares found buying support after Dow rise and on market rumours it could declare a special dividend.
Bellwether issue had mixed session but ended weaker after its ADRs slipped in New York on Friday.
Gold issues found renewed buying interest after the price of gold recovered slightly from recent falls on Friday.
Cyclical transport and media shares led the market higher after the Dow's rise and on investor hopes of a rate cut.
